```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Anchor here() to this post so paths work no matter where R starts
here::i_am("posts/kitchener-phone-wait-times/index.qmd")

# House colours, ggplot2 theme, and the packages every post uses
source(here::here("R", "theme_cwr.R"))

# Data download bundle helpers; data_bundle_version is the release version linked at the end.
# Bump it when the data changes and /publish rebuilds the bundle.
source(here::here("R", "data_bundle.R"))
data_bundle_version <- 1
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false

# One row per day, one column per metric; produced by R/02_clean_data.R
queue_daily <- read_csv(
  here("posts", "kitchener-phone-wait-times", "data", "queue_daily.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(month = factor(month, levels = month.abb))

# The contact centre runs a skeleton service on weekends and holidays (about a
# third of the weekday call volume), so every number below is weekdays only.
weekday <- queue_daily |>
  filter(!weekend_or_holiday)

# "Within target" throughout means answered within 30 seconds, counting a call
# that was abandoned while waiting as a miss: the strictest of the four
# versions the City reports.
pct_within <- function(answered, presented) 100 * sum(answered) / sum(presented)

yearly <- weekday |>
  summarise(
    days          = n(),
    calls_per_day = mean(calls_presented),
    pct_within    = pct_within(answered_within_target, calls_presented),
    pct_abandoned = 100 * sum(calls_abandoned) / sum(calls_presented),
    avg_wait      = weighted.mean(avg_queue_time, calls_presented),
    .by = year
  )

monthly <- weekday |>
  summarise(
    calls      = sum(calls_presented),
    pct_within = pct_within(answered_within_target, calls_presented),
    avg_wait   = weighted.mean(avg_queue_time, calls_presented),
    .by = year_month
  )

# Average weekday across all years, by month of the year (seasonality)
by_month <- weekday |>
  summarise(
    calls_per_day = mean(calls_presented),
    pct_within    = pct_within(answered_within_target, calls_presented),
    .by = month
  ) |>
  arrange(month)

# Numbers quoted in the text, pulled from the tables above so they cannot drift
first_year <- min(yearly$year)
last_year  <- max(yearly$year)
yr <- function(y, col) yearly |> filter(year == y) |> pull({{ col }})
pct_first <- yr(first_year, pct_within)
pct_2022  <- yr(2022, pct_within)
pct_last  <- yr(last_year, pct_within)
wait_first <- yr(first_year, avg_wait)
wait_2022  <- yr(2022, avg_wait)
wait_last  <- yr(last_year, avg_wait)
calls_first <- yr(first_year, calls_per_day)
calls_last  <- yr(last_year, calls_per_day)
calls_change_pct <- 100 * (calls_last / calls_first - 1)
best_month  <- monthly |> slice_max(pct_within, n = 1)
worst_month <- monthly |> slice_min(pct_within, n = 1)
busiest  <- by_month |> slice_max(calls_per_day, n = 1)
quietest <- by_month |> slice_min(calls_per_day, n = 1)
weekend_share <- queue_daily |>
  summarise(calls = mean(calls_presented), .by = weekend_or_holiday) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = weekend_or_holiday, values_from = calls) |>
  mutate(share = `TRUE` / `FALSE`) |>
  pull(share)

# Formatting helpers for the prose
pct <- label_number(accuracy = 1, suffix = "%")
secs <- label_number(accuracy = 1, suffix = " seconds")
mon <- \(d) format(d, "%B %Y")
```

Call the City of Kitchener on a weekday and the odds of someone picking up within half a minute have fallen from `r pct(pct_first)` in `r first_year` to `r pct(pct_last)` in `r last_year`. The average wait in the queue went from `r secs(wait_first)` to `r secs(wait_last)`. Call volumes barely moved over the same period, so the slowdown is not a story about more people phoning in.

## The 80% target held until 2021, then slipped

The City measures itself against a common contact-centre yardstick: answer 80% of calls within 30 seconds. On weekdays in `r first_year` it met that target almost exactly. Through the first two pandemic years it stayed close, with the best months of all in the quiet January and February of 2020 and 2021, when more than `r pct(floor(best_month$pct_within))` of calls were answered on time.

The break came in 2022. Every month that year was below target, and `r mon(worst_month$year_month)` was the low point, with `r pct(worst_month$pct_within)` of calls answered within 30 seconds. The first seven months of 2023 look much like 2022.

```{r}
#| label: answered
#| output: asis

# ggline (single series) with a target line; the target is explained in the
# subtitle rather than a label so nothing collides on the phone version
p <- ggplot(monthly, aes(x = year_month, y = pct_within)) +

  # the City's target, drawn first so the data line sits on top of it
  geom_hline(yintercept = 80, colour = habsred, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5) +

  geom_line(colour = dodgerblue, linewidth = 0.8) +

  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 year",
    date_labels = "%Y",
    date_minor_breaks = "3 months",
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(50, 100),
    breaks = seq(50, 100, 10),
    labels = label_number(suffix = "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
    position = "right"
  ) +

  guides(x = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +

  # Right-axis label positioning: sit labels above gridlines
  theme(
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(
      size = rel(1),
      hjust = 1.0,
      vjust = -0.5,
      margin = margin(r = 12, l = -30)
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Calls answered within 30 seconds fell below target in 2022 and stayed there",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Share of weekday calls answered within 30 seconds, by month. ",
      "<span style='color:", habsred, "'>Dashed line: the City's 80% target</span><br>"
    ),
    caption = cwr_caption("City of Kitchener Open Data")
  )

cwr_figure(
  p, "fig-answered",
  caption = "Share of weekday calls to the City of Kitchener answered within 30 seconds, by month, March 2019 to July 2023.",
  alt = "Line chart of the monthly share of calls answered within 30 seconds. The line sits near the 80% target through 2019, 2020 and 2021 with a dip in mid-2020, then drops below the target for all of 2022 and 2023, reaching a low near 60% in May 2022.",
  height = 5, phone_height = 4.5
)
```

## The average wait more than doubled

Averages hide a lot in a phone queue, since most calls are answered quickly and a few wait a very long time. Even so, the direction is clear. A weekday caller in `r first_year` waited `r secs(wait_first)` on average. In 2022 that was `r secs(wait_2022)`, and the first seven months of `r last_year` averaged `r secs(wait_last)`.

Volume does not explain it. The centre handled `r label_number(accuracy = 1)(calls_first)` calls on a typical weekday in `r first_year` and `r label_number(accuracy = 1)(calls_last)` in `r last_year`, a rise of `r pct(calls_change_pct)`. The data says nothing about staffing, which is the obvious place to look next.

```{r}
#| label: wait
#| output: asis

# ggvertbar with direct labels in place of the value axis
plot_data <- yearly |>
  mutate(
    year_label = if_else(year == last_year, paste0(year, "\n(to July)"), as.character(year)),
    year_label = fct_inorder(year_label),
    # the two years since the target was missed are the focus
    focus = year >= 2022
  )

p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = year_label, y = avg_wait, fill = focus)) +

  geom_col(width = 0.7) +

  geom_text(
    aes(label = label_number(accuracy = 1, suffix = " s")(avg_wait)),
    nudge_y = 2,
    vjust = 0,
    size = label_size,
    colour = "grey30"
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(`TRUE` = dodgerblue, `FALSE` = cowboysilver),
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))) +

  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +

  # bars carry their values, so the value axis and gridlines go
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "The average wait in the queue more than doubled",
    subtitle = "Average seconds a weekday caller waited before being answered or hanging up",
    caption = cwr_caption("City of Kitchener Open Data")
  )

cwr_figure(
  p, "fig-wait",
  caption = "Average time a weekday caller spent waiting in the City of Kitchener phone queue, by year. 2023 covers January to July.",
  alt = "Bar chart of average queue time by year: about 26 seconds in 2019, 29 in 2020, 37 in 2021, 63 in 2022 and 58 in the first seven months of 2023.",
  height = 4, phone_height = 3.8
)
```

## Early summer is the crunch

Whatever the year, the phones are busiest in `r month.name[busiest$month]` and quietest in `r month.name[quietest$month]`, and the answer rate follows the volume: over the whole period, `r pct(by_month |> filter(month == busiest$month) |> pull(pct_within))` of June calls were answered on time against `r pct(by_month |> filter(month == "Jan") |> pull(pct_within))` in January. Property tax bills, summer recreation registration and moving season all land in the same few weeks. A centre that just meets its target in a quiet month will miss it in a busy one unless staffing moves with the calendar.

```{r}
#| label: season
#| output: asis

# ggvertbar, busiest two months highlighted, direct labels in place of the value axis
plot_data <- by_month |>
  mutate(busy = month %in% c("Jun", "Jul"))

p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = month, y = calls_per_day, fill = busy)) +

  geom_col(width = 0.7) +

  geom_text(
    aes(label = label_number(accuracy = 1)(calls_per_day)),
    nudge_y = 6,
    vjust = 0,
    size = label_size,
    colour = "grey30"
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(`TRUE` = dodgerblue, `FALSE` = cowboysilver),
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.03))) +

  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +

  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "June brings a third more calls than December",
    subtitle = "Average calls per weekday, by month of the year, 2019 to 2023",
    caption = cwr_caption("City of Kitchener Open Data")
  )

cwr_figure(
  p, "fig-season",
  caption = "Average number of calls presented to the City of Kitchener phone queue on a weekday, by month of the year, March 2019 to July 2023.",
  alt = "Bar chart of average weekday calls by month of the year. Calls climb from under 300 a day in December and January to a peak near 400 in June, then fall through the autumn. June and July are highlighted.",
  height = 4, phone_height = 4
)
```

## Data and methods

The City of Kitchener publishes daily metrics for its main phone queue on its open data portal. This post uses the export covering 26 February 2019 to 30 July 2023, the full range available when it was downloaded in February 2025. Days with an incomplete or duplicated set of metrics (14 of about 1,600) and the partial first month were dropped.

All figures are weekdays excluding Ontario statutory holidays. Weekend and holiday volumes run at roughly `r pct(100 * weekend_share)` of a weekday, on a reduced service, and would flatter every average.

"Answered within 30 seconds" is the share of all calls presented that an agent picked up inside the target, so a caller who hung up while waiting counts as a miss. The City also reports three gentler versions of the same measure, all included in the download below. Waits are the daily average queue time weighted by the number of calls that day.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
